parsed.title: Simulation and Synthesized Data in Training and Evaluating Driving Policies
outline: Introduction to simulation and mid-level representations
End-to-end learning approaches in autonomous driving
Simulation platforms supporting training and evaluation
Gap in comparative evaluation of driving methods
parsed.markdown: Simulation environments and mid-level representations are used to train autonomous driving models on both real and simulated data, enabling closed-loop simulation testing prior to real-world deployment [1]. The CARLA simulator is an open-source platform that supports the development, training, and validation of autonomous urban driving systems, allowing flexible specification of sensor suites and environmental conditions [2]. End-to-end learning approaches have been explored, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs) that learn the entire processing pipeline to steer a vehicle using input from a single front-facing center camera [3]. CARLA has been used to study multiple autonomous driving approaches, including classic modular pipelines, end-to-end imitation learning, and end-to-end reinforcement learning [2]. ChauffeurNet is a recurrent neural network (RNN) that uses mid-level input representations to output driving trajectories for vehicle control [1]. However, there is no direct comparative evaluation reported between end-to-end CNN approaches and RNN-based mid-level methods like ChauffeurNet under the same conditions or metrics, indicating a gap in understanding their relative performance.
